items.title: Why We Prefer Alphabet Stock Over Meta Right Now
items.summary: Our Monday piece, Should You Be Worried About Meta Stock?, opened on a split result: Meta Platforms (META) grew revenue 26% in its September quarter, yet its operating income fell 37%. The fall came from one item, a $9.9 billion legal charge; without it, the company says operating income would have risen 11%. So the next question is the one an owner of either AI giant asks: if you are buying one of them now, Meta or Alphabet (GOOGL.

items.title: Why Analysts Expect Nearly 7% More Than Take-Two Does
items.summary: Our latest piece, Could A GTA VI That Meets Guidance Hurt Take-Two Stock?, started from an odd quarter: fiscal second-quarter net bookings of $1.6 billion came in below the company's own $1.62 billion to $1.67 billion range, yet the shares rose 8.3% the next day. That piece left a question open: why do analysts expect more revenue this year than Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO) says it will deliver.

items.title: Is Nutanix Stock Really Cheap At 11x Earnings?
items.summary: Nutanix (NTNX) closed at $58.94 on Monday, Nov 16, which works out to 11.4 times its reported fiscal 2026 earnings of $5.17 a share. That looks like a bargain for a software company. It is not. About 79.6% of last year's reported profit came from a one-time $1.2 billion tax benefit, and once you take it out the stock trades at 56.7 times earnings.
